title: Colombia quake leaves more than 110 dead – as it happened
text: 3d ago 01.04 EDT Closing summary We’re about to wrap up this live coverage of Colombia’s devastating earthquake but you can read an updated full report here – and below is a recap of the day’s news. It’s now a little after midnight local time. Search and rescue efforts were under way early on Tuesday in dozens of cities and towns in western Colombia after a powerful earthquake struck the region. At least 110 people were killed after the 7.4-magnitude quake struck on Monday morning local time, toppling buildings, damaging hospitals and infrastructure and trapping people beneath the rubble in Colombia’s strongest earthquake this century. More than 2,700 people had been reported missing by Monday night. New president Abelardo de la Espriella – sworn in just days earlier – declared a state of emergency and said in an address to the nation that his government had deployed all of its capabilities “to protect lives, assist affected ‌communities and deliver aid wherever it is needed”. “The first priority is rescuing the people trapped under the rubble,” de la Espriella said after about 1,600 buildings had been damaged , including at least 61 that completely collapsed. text: Russia using North Korean missiles to strike Ukraine, Zelensky says Image source, Reuters By Dan Johnson ,Â Reporting from Kyiv Â and Â Tom McArthur Published 11 August 2026 Ukraine and Russia have continued striking each other overnight, with President Volodymyr Zelensky accusing Moscow of using North Korean missiles. text: Russian Wheat Exports Brace for Decade Low in August Amid Black Sea Attacks Aug. 11, 2026 A combine in Russia's Rostov Region harvests wheat. REUTERS / Sergei Pivovarov Russian grain exports risk dropping to a decade low in August due to shipping bottlenecks in southern ports caused by escalating attacks on commercial vessels in the Black Sea, industry analysts warned Tuesday. Agricultural consultancy SovEcon projects Russia will export between 3 million and 3.4 million metric tons of wheat this month — well below the five-year August average of 5 million tons and potentially marking the lowest August total since the 2016–17 agricultural season. Independent consultancy ProZerno, meanwhile, forecasts that overall grain exports will fall to nearly 2.5 million metric tons amid severe congestion across the Black Sea and the Sea of Azov. The five-year August average for grain exports is 5.7 million tons. title: Russia Says Syria Base Deal Will Boost Ties, Source Says Some Russian Forces Will Stay
text: Russia Says Syria Base Deal Will Boost Ties, Source Says Some Russian Forces Will Stay By Reuters Aug. 11, 2026 Russian servicemen at the Khmeimim air base, 2023. Russia's Defense Ministry Russia's Foreign Ministry said on Tuesday that a deal reached with Syria on the future of Moscow's military bases in the country would boost ties between the nations, and a Syrian source said some Russian forces would still be stationed there under the agreement. Syria's state news agency cited the Syrian Foreign Ministry on Sunday as saying Syria and Russia had reached a memorandum of understanding to settle the future of Russian bases at Tartus and Khmeimim. The bases' future became uncertain after Russian ally Bashar al-Assad fled the country in 2024. The memorandum followed 18 months of intensive negotiations. The ministry was quoted as saying the Syrian state would take over management of civilian facilities, including Khmeimim airport and the commercial berth at Tartus port, allowing them to gradually integrate into the country's civilian administration. Military facilities would be repurposed as joint training centers, with the transition to be completed within three months. Bases help Mos

Russia's Defense Ministry Russia's Foreign Ministry said on Tuesday that a deal reached with Syria on the future of Moscow's military bases in the country would boost ties between the nations, and a Syrian source said some Russian forces would still be stationed there under the agreement. Syria's state news agency cited the Syrian Foreign Ministry on Sunday as saying Syria and Russia had reached a memorandum of understanding to settle the future of Russian bases at Tartus and Khmeimim. The bases' future became uncertain after Russian ally Bashar al-Assad fled the country in 2024. The memorandum followed 18 months of intensive negotiations. The ministry was quoted as saying the Syrian state would take over management of civilian facilities, including Khmeimim airport and the commercial berth at Tartus port, allowing them to gradually integrate into the country's civilian administration. title: As Russia Strips Rights from Exiled Regime Opponents, Many Don’t Know if They Should Worry
text: As Russia Strips Rights from Exiled Regime Opponents, Many Don’t Know if They Should Worry By Brawley Benson Aug. 11, 2026 A rally against the war in Ukraine in Paris. Mathias Reding / pexels If living in forced exile outside of your home country isn’t hard enough, imagine not being able to withdraw money from your bank accounts or renew your passport. With the stroke of a pen, President Vladimir Putin approved a law imposing sweeping restrictions on thousands of exiled regime critics last week, cutting them off from basic consular services and impeding their ability to manage personal affairs back home. The list of prohibited activities includes managing one’s finances, properties and legal matters. Bank accounts will be frozen, embassies will refuse most appointments, and people to whom the law applies won’t even be able to use the government’s digital services portal or do something as simple as register a marriage . Human rights organizations have decried the new measures as an attempt to further hamstring Russian political exiles, many of whom fled Russia due to increased wartime repression. title: Russia’s Central Bank Proposes Framework for Publicly Trading Major Cryptocurrencies
text: Russia’s Central Bank Proposes Framework for Publicly Trading Major Cryptocurrencies Aug. 11, 2026 Ivan Babydov / pexels Russia’s Central Bank on Tuesday proposed allowing investors to trade Bitcoin, Ether and Tether on official Russian exchanges, establishing a regulated infrastructure for cryptocurrency trading set to take effect next month. The rules would expand on a law President Vladimir Putin signed this month, which formally legalizes cryptocurrency trading in Russia. Starting Sept. 1, both retail and professional investors will be required to pass a test before trading the three major cryptocurrencies. The Central Bank says retail investors currently account for about 98% of market participants. Cryptocurrencies will be allowed in cross-border settlements but banned as payment methods inside Russia under the new law. The Central Bank said it selected the three major cryptocurrencies based on requirements that they have a minimum five-year price history on foreign platforms, as well as high liquidity and market capitalization. title: Putin Pardons Former U.S. Marine Imprisoned in Russia – Reuters
text: Putin Pardons Former U.S. Marine Imprisoned in Russia – Reuters Aug. 11, 2026 Former U.S. Marine Robert Gilman. REUTERS / Vladimir Lavrov Moscow has freed Robert Gilman, a former U.S. Marine and English teacher imprisoned in Russia, after President Vladimir Putin approved a pardon for the ailing American based on humanitarian reasons, Reuters reported Tuesday, citing U.S. officials. Gilman’s release comes after his family had appealed to the Russian authorities for his release, warning that he was “near death” following months of alleged torture in prison. U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio was also said to have raised Gilman’s imprisonment with Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov during a meeting in the Philippines last month. U.S. officials told Reuters that Gilman, who was said to be walking and talking, would be transported on a State Department plane from Russia to Washington Dulles Airport. “ All things considered, he seems to be in good shape, ” one official told the news agency. title: Mongolia Says Russia Agreed to Send Emergency Fuel Supplies Amid Shortages
text: Mongolia Says Russia Agreed to Send Emergency Fuel Supplies Amid Shortages Aug. 11, 2026 Yaroslav Chingaev / Moskva News Agency Russia has agreed to provide Mongolia with additional shipments of gasoline and jet fuel to help relieve a fuel shortage that officials in the landlocked country have blamed on high seasonal demand, Mongolian officials said late Monday. Mongolian Industry Minister Gongoryn Damdinnyam said Russia committed to delivering an extra 25,000 metric tons of AI-92 gasoline and 5,000 metric tons of jet fuel by the end of August. “I express my gratitude to the Russian government and its businesses for their assistance in helping us overcome this unprecedented difficult period,” he wrote in a post on X following talks with Russian officials and executives from Rosneft and Gazprom. Russia accounts for up to 97% of Mongolia’s gasoline and diesel imports. title: One Killed in Ukrainian Attack on Wildberries Logistics Center in Voronezh
text: One Killed in Ukrainian Attack on Wildberries Logistics Center in Voronezh Aug. 11, 2026 Smoke rising into the morning sky in the Voronezh region on Aug. 11, 2026. @exilenova_plus / Telegram A Ukrainian drone attack killed one person and injured two others in the southwestern Voronezh region, local officials said Tuesday, with online retailer Wildberries saying that a fire broke out at one of its logistics centers during the air assault. Voronezh region Governor Alexander Gusev said a 49-year-old man died after being hospitalized for injuries he sustained from falling drone debris. He said two others, one of whom had been at a “large logistics center” during the attack, remained hospitalized. Wildberries confirmed that its logistics center was struck and said it evacuated all of its employees. The company later said firefighters managed to put out a blaze that erupted at the facility, adding that “most” of the goods stored there were undamaged. title: Russia using North Korean missiles to strike Ukraine, Zelensky says
text: Russia using North Korean missiles to strike Ukraine, Zelensky says Image source, Reuters By Dan Johnson ,Â Reporting from Kyiv Â and Â Tom McArthur Published 11 August 2026 Ukraine and Russia have continued striking each other overnight, with President Volodymyr Zelensky accusing Moscow of using North Korean missiles. Ukraine said strikes on the southern city of Zaporizhzhia - which killed seven people and injured at least 24 - involved ballistic missiles from Russia's ally. In Voronezh, western Russia, warehouses of the biggest online retailer Wildberries were hit by Ukraine. The company, known as Russia's Amazon, has been repeatedly targeted in recent weeks. The attacks come a day after at least 13 people were killed, including one child, in Ukrainian drone strikes on the Russian republic of Tatarstan, more than 1,100 km (680 miles) from the Ukrainian border. In a video address on Monday evening, Zelensky said "for the first time" Russia "cannot wage war without reinforcements from North Korea". title: Russian Wheat Exports Brace for Decade Low in August Amid Black Sea Attacks
text: Russian Wheat Exports Brace for Decade Low in August Amid Black Sea Attacks Aug. 11, 2026 A combine in Russia's Rostov Region harvests wheat. REUTERS / Sergei Pivovarov Russian grain exports risk dropping to a decade low in August due to shipping bottlenecks in southern ports caused by escalating attacks on commercial vessels in the Black Sea, industry analysts warned Tuesday. Agricultural consultancy SovEcon projects Russia will export between 3 million and 3.4 million metric tons of wheat this month — well below the five-year August average of 5 million tons and potentially marking the lowest August total since the 2016–17 agricultural season. Independent consultancy ProZerno, meanwhile, forecasts that overall grain exports will fall to nearly 2.5 million metric tons amid severe congestion across the Black Sea and the Sea of Azov. The five-year August average for grain exports is 5.7 million tons. Russia , the world’s largest wheat exporter, and Ukraine, also a major agricultural exporter, have been attacking each other’s agricultural export facilities and commercial vessels in the Black Sea area in recent weeks, driving wheat prices higher on global markets. title: Fast and fearless: Baltic defence startups innovate to counter Russian threat
text: Advertising Fast and fearless: Baltic defence startups innovate to counter Russian threat Analysis Europe As the nature of Russia’s war in Ukraine evolves, Baltic startups are seeking new ways to respond to the hybrid threat from Russia, hoping rapid innovation can have a deterrent effect on Moscow. But they may also herald a new dystopian future, where ordinary civilians become targets of flying objects manned by faraway operators.
